headline: Ward 19 ranks 7th of 50 citywide, though several top scores rest on modeled estimates.
summary:
Ward 19 covers Beverly, Mount Greenwood, Morgan Park and Auburn Gresham on the far southwest side. It ranks 7th of 50 wards overall, one of the higher scores in the report. The strongest numbers include the lowest measured proximity to hazardous-waste facilities of any ward, the highest share of aldermanic menu money spent on street resurfacing (99.6 percent), and the highest voter turnout in the city (62 percent of registered voters). A separate set of top scores comes from modeled estimates of resident satisfaction and safety rather than an actual local survey.

The weaker numbers describe a different kind of place. Ward 19 has the fewest grocery stores per resident of any ward, just over one per 10,000 people, and ranks near the bottom for licensed entertainment venues, fine-particulate air pollution, ride-share spending, and the share of workers who commute by public transit (9.2 percent, third lowest in the city). Together, the numbers describe a mostly residential part of the city built more around driving than transit or retail.
reading_the_rankings: Ward 19's rank of first for voter turnout is a straight count, 62 percent of registered voters cast a ballot, the highest share of any ward, tallied against the ward's current 2023 boundaries rather than the different-shaped ward that existed in earlier elections. Its rank of 50th, dead last, on menu spending diversity looks damning next to that, but the caveat attached to the measure says the opposite: it only tracks how spread out the aldermanic infrastructure budget is across project types, and the source itself notes that concentrating money in one category isn't better or worse than spreading it around. A rank of 49th on entertainment venues carries a similar warning: 16 other wards land within two points of this ward's score, and the whole city is bunched into a 10-point range on this measure, so a rank in the high 40s reflects a small gap in a crowded field, not real distance from the middle of the pack.

news.headline: As Beverly Speed Cameras Continue To Rack Up Tickets, One Camera Could Be On The Move
news.note: The 19th Ward's lowest-ticketing speed camera, on 99th Street, may move to a stretch near two schools on 111th Street after parents raised safety concerns.

news.headline: Original Rainbow Cone Hosting 100th Birthday Bash Sunday
news.note: The Beverly ice cream shop on Western Avenue is marking its 100th year with a birthday party, cake, and prize giveaways.

news.headline: Horse Thief Hollow's Barrel-Aged Brew Wins Gold At U.S. Beer Championships
news.note: The Beverly brewery won a national gold medal for a Belgian-style beer that spent more than two years aging in oak barrels.
